title: GRIT: Enhancing Multi-GPU Performance with Fine-Grained Dynamic Page Placement
problem: Multi-GPU systems with unified virtual memory suffer from NUMA overhead due to data sharing across GPUs. No single page placement scheme (on-touch migration, access counter-based migration, or page duplication) works well across all applications, pages, and execution phases.
motivation: Optimizing memory access patterns is critical for achieving performance scalability in multi-GPU systems.
method: GRIT watches how your program accesses memory as it runs, then dynamically picks the best placement strategy for each page (a chunk of memory) at each moment. It chooses between three options: moving pages to where they're being used (on-touch migration), moving frequently-used pages to better locations (access counter-based migration), or keeping copies in multiple places (page duplication). The system adapts based on which approach actually performs best.
key_novelty: GRIT dynamically selects the best memory placement strategy for each page and execution phase based on observed behavior, rather than using one strategy for everything.
contributions: Identifies that optimal page placement strategy varies across applications, pages, and execution phases
Proposes GRIT system for dynamic fine-grained page placement scheme selection
Demonstrates 29-60% speedup improvements over uniform page placement strategies

metrics.speedup: 60% vs on-touch migration, 49% vs access counter-based, 29% vs page duplication

primary_theme: Dynamic memory page placement for multi-GPU performance
